context: Replacing offset-based pagination in list_orders with keyset (cursor) pagination based on the last-seen order id.
explanation: This fixes the classic offset-pagination problem: with OFFSET, a row inserted or deleted between two page fetches shifts later pages, so rows get skipped or duplicated. Keyset pagination (WHERE id > after_id ORDER BY id LIMIT n) is stable regardless of concurrent writes. It also fetches page_size + 1 rows to determine has_more in the same query instead of a separate COUNT(*), and clamps page_size to MAX_PAGE_SIZE so a caller can't request an unbounded page. The returned items/next_cursor shape is a standard, self-describing cursor response.
